record.original_question: Are the single-machine throughput problems 1|r_j|sum U_j and 1|r_j|sum w_j U_j W[1]-hard when parameterized by p_max, the maximum processing time?

evidence.quote: Open Problem 3. Are 1|rj |ΣUj and 1|rj |ΣwjUj W[1]-hard parameterized by the maximum processing time pmax?
Release dates. Each job j may have a release date rj, before which it cannot be started. In this case, we add “rj” to the β-field.

If each job j ∈ J has a due date dj ∈ N, we also minimize – the total weighted tardiness P j∈J wjT j, where T j = max{0, dj − Cj}, and – the weighted number of tardy jobs, P j∈J wjUj, where Uj = 0 if job j is finished by its due date and Uj = 1 otherwise. This is equivalent to maximizing throughput—the weighted number of jobs that get finished by their due dates.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider single-machine scheduling problems in standard three-field notation. There is one machine and a set J of n jobs. Each job j ∈ J has a processing time p_j ∈ ℕ, a release date r_j ∈ ℕ (so job j cannot start before time r_j), a due date d_j ∈ ℕ, and (in the weighted variant) a weight w_j ∈ ℕ. A schedule assigns each job j a start time S_j ≥ r_j on the single machine such that the time intervals [S_j, S_j + p_j) for distinct jobs are pairwise disjoint; the completion time is C_j = S_j + p_j. Define U_j = 0 if C_j ≤ d_j and U_j = 1 otherwise.

Let p_max = max_{j ∈ J} p_j.

Consider the parameterized decision problems:
(a) 1|r_j|∑U_j: given the instance and an integer k, decide whether there exists a feasible schedule with ∑_{j ∈ J} U_j ≤ k, parameterized by p_max.
(b) 1|r_j|∑w_j U_j: given the instance and an integer k, decide whether there exists a feasible schedule with ∑_{j ∈ J} w_j U_j ≤ k, parameterized by p_max.

Question: Are problems (a) and (b) W[1]-hard with respect to the parameter p_max?
artifact.status_search_result: Recent works (Heeger–Hermelin, ESA 2024; an IPEC 2024 paper on 1|r_j|∑w_j U_j with release dates) study the parameterized complexity of 1|r_j|∑w_j U_j, establishing W[1]-hardness for parameters such as the number of distinct processing times p_# or weights w_#, and FPT results for various combinations of p_#, w_#, d_#, r_#. However, none of the located sources resolve W[1]-hardness when the parameter is the maximum processing time p_max itself; this specific parameterization appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Single-Machine Scheduling to Minimize the Number of Tardy Jobs with Release Dates
status_evidence.snippet: Heeger and Hermelin [ESA, 2024] recently showed (weak) W[1]-hardness parameterized by p_# or w_#... FPT parameterized by p_# combined with any two of the remaining three parameters w_#, d_#, r_#.
status_evidence.claim: Recent results address parameterizations by numbers of distinct processing times/weights/due dates/release dates, but not by p_max.

status_evidence.title: Minimizing the Weighted Number of Tardy Jobs is W[1]-hard
status_evidence.snippet: Minimizing the Weighted Number of Tardy Jobs Is W[1]-hard (parameterized by number of distinct processing times).
status_evidence.claim: W[1]-hardness is known for the parameter p_# (number of distinct processing times), a different parameter than p_max.
